title: Larkspur Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
next_steps: Send onboarding playbook and SSO + SAML configuration guide
Provision staging dedicated capacity for 2-week pilot
Share SOC2 and data handling docs via secure link
action_items: Maya Patel: Send onboarding docs and pricing - due 2027-05-03
Priya Nair: Provide VPC network diagram and firewall rules / IP allowlist - due 2027-04-29
Ethan Green: Run initial latency benchmark with sample dataset and share results - due 2027-05-05
summary: Kickoff for Larkspur Health onboarding. Covered success criteria, integration plan, security requirements (SSO, KMS, SOC2), and pilot scope (staging dedicated capacity + latency benchmarks). Agreed on next steps and owners.
transcript: 00:00 Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. We also have Ethan from solutions and Diego from our CSM team. 00:14 Sarah Cho: Hey thanks, Sarah here. Excited to get started. Quick background - we're rolling Redwood into our triage and summarization pipeline for clinical notes, goal is to reduce manual review and speed up throughput. 00:29 Maya Patel: Awesome, can you remind us of the top success metrics? latency, cost per token, accuracy? 00:36 Michael Reyes: Main ones are throughput - we need to process about 200k notes per day eventually, latency for interactive flows around 300-500ms tail, and of course PHI handling and audits are critical. 00:50 Ethan Green: Got it. Sounds like a good fit for a staged approach: start with hosted sandbox to validate prompts, then move to staging on Dedicated for perf tests, then Private if you need VPC isolation. 01:05 Priya Nair: Our security team will push for VPC and KMS. We also have strict egress rules, so IP allowlisting and SAML SSO are required. 01:15 Diego Ramos: That's common - we'll share our SSO guide and the KMS integration doc. We support customer-managed KMS and HSM via our Private deploy. 01:28 Omar Bello: On the model side, are you recommending a specific variant for summarization? We worry about hallucinations and medical terminology. 01:36 Ethan Green: For clinical summarization we typically recommend our curated M-2 series (note: sometimes labelled 'med-lite' in older docs) - it balances quality and cost. We'll also provide a regression test harness so you can run evals on your prompt sets. 01:52 Michael Reyes: Cool. Can we quantize or do 8-bit to reduce footprint? 01:58 Ethan Green: Yes, we support quantized variants. We'll list recommended quant profiles per throughput target. There is sometimes a small quality delta; that's why the eval harness is important. 02:10 Sarah Cho: Timeline - we want pilot in prod in 8 weeks. Is that realistic? 02:16 Maya Patel: Yes, if we start now. Week 1 config and SSO, week 2 prompt tuning and small-scale integration, week 3-4 dedicated perf tests, week 5 pilot rollout, week 6-8 monitor + iterate. 02:30 Priya Nair: Who will own network setup? Our infra team or Redwood? 02:34 Maya Patel: You'll own VPC peering and firewall, we'll provide network requirements, IP ranges, and coordinate with your infra. Diego will be the point for handoffs. 02:44 Diego Ramos: I'll coordinate and set up the onboarding playbook tasks in our tracker. 02:50 Michael Reyes: What about auditing - we need audit logs and data residency info for compliance. 02:55 Diego Ramos: We have per-request audit logs and configurable retention. For Private deployments we can host logs in customer account or ship them to your SIEM. We'll send the SOC2 and ISO docs after the call. 03:09 Priya Nair: Any gotchas with KV cache and stateful sessions? Our app maintains conversation state per patient. 03:15 Ethan Green: Our runtime supports KV cache and session pinning. For patient-level context we recommend prefix caching with TTLs; we'll share best practices. Note that caching can reduce cost but you need careful invalidation for PHI. 03:30 Omar Bello: Great. On benchmarking - will you run benchmarks or do we? 03:34 Ethan Green: We can run an initial benchmark if you share a representative sample (anonymized). We'll run latency and token-cost analyses on staging Dedicated hardware (NVIDIA H200 / A100 variants). We can also provide a runbook for you to reproduce. 03:50 Sarah Cho: Speaking of hardware - if we need predictable throughput what's the Dedicated commitment? 03:55 Maya Patel: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with SLAs. For pilot we recommend a small reserve and burst capacity. We'll send an estimated cost sheet after we scope the expected qps and sequence length. 04:08 Michael Reyes: Competitors - we've looked at Anthropic for safety features and OpenAI for developer ergonomics. Any notes? 04:16 Maya Patel: We often see customers compare those. Redwood focuses on production controls (batching, routing, cost controls) and unified deployment (hosted -> dedicated -> private) which simplifies rollouts. We'll share a short comparison doc. 04:30 Sarah Cho: On access controls, we need RBAC and SSO. 04:33 Diego Ramos: We support SAML/SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. We'll include setup guide. 04:45 Priya Nair: Encryption at rest - how does KMS work? 04:49 Ethan Green: For Private you can bring your own KMS, or we can integrate with cloud KMS. We don't store unencrypted payloads outside the configured KMS; we'll share architecture diagram. 05:00 Michael Reyes: Any recommended logging retention policy? 05:03 Diego Ramos: Typical customers keep 90 days of request logs and token-level traces for 30 days. If you need longer we can arrange archival to your S3. 05:12 Sarah Cho: Ok great. Let's talk immediate tasks. 05:15 Maya Patel: Recap of next steps: Maya will send onboarding playbook, security docs, and price estimate; Priya will send network diagram; Ethan will run benchmarks once sample is received; Diego will set up the project tracker and invite stakeholders. 05:30 Omar Bello: Quick question about model rollouts - can we do canary A/B? 05:34 Ethan Green: Yes, our Console supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies. We'll show that in the workshop. 05:44 Michael Reyes: Perfect. Anything else on compliance checklist? 05:47 Priya Nair: We also need a signed DPA. 05:49 Maya Patel: We'll send the standard DPA and escalate if needed. 05:52 Diego Ramos: I'll attach it to the follow-up email along with SOC2. 05:58 Sarah Cho: Thanks everyone. 06:00 Maya Patel: Thanks team - we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the workshop. Diego will reach out with calendar invites. 06:07 (end)
